page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a memory-optimized instance in the VX1 Cloud Compute line. Built on AMD EPYC architecture, the configuration pairs 24 physical cores across 48 dedicated virtual threads clocked at 2.0 GHz with 384 GB of system memory. This yields an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Storage is bundled directly as a 2880 GB local NVMe SSD array, and connectivity includes a single assigned public IPv4 address. The server operates entirely on CPU resources without dedicated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate exceptional memory bandwidth and robust integer processing. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 414.9 GB/sec, placing it in the top decile, while large-block write bandwidth sustains 213.09 GB/sec. The instance delivers a Geekbench single-core score of 2,771 and a multi-core score of 26,345, complemented by top-tier single-threaded compression performance at 40.56 GB/sec in gzip. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, enabling competent CPU-based vector calculations. In-memory data handling is confirmed by 85.37 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database scores.

The dense allocation of 384 GB RAM combined with local high-speed NVMe storage delivers high resource efficiency for data platforms that do not require specialized GPU accelerators. However, the 2.0 GHz base clock speed represents a tradeoff for workloads that rely heavily on single-thread clock frequency rather than parallel throughput or memory capacity. While CPU-based LLM inference functions adequately on small parameter models, token generation drops noticeably on larger 70-billion parameter models, confirming this system is tailored primarily for high-density caching, large relational or in-memory databases, Clang compilation pipelines, and transactional enterprise data processing.
description: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical AMD EPYC cores) operating at 2.0 GHz, 384 GB of RAM, and 2880 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on an x86_64 architecture with 32 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 support, the system provides an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier large-block memory read bandwidth of 414.9 GB/sec, top-tier single-core and multi-core Geekbench ratings, and over 85 million Redis operations per second. The server omits discrete GPU hardware, relying on substantial memory capacity and fast direct-attached storage for efficient data-heavy processing. vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is best suited for memory-bound relational engines, large in-memory caches, data analytics pipelines, and multi-threaded compilation suites.
